parts.note: bum is slang for bad or wrong, as in a bum note
F is the standard abbreviation for folio

explanation.surface: A misplaced page has turned up among some government documents.
explanation.walkthrough: BUMF is British slang for tedious paperwork; the word began as a crude term for toilet paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is informal British slang for unwanted forms, memos and bureaucratic documents, which official papers describes.

clue.text: Monstrous creature initially bought the home in a devious way

indicators.note: something devious takes a twisting path, so the letters are jumbled
initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of this word
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monster first purchased a house by underhand means.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth is a huge biblical beast, and the word now names any monstrous creature.

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: misery is great suffering

explanation.surface: A tightwad brings constant pain to those around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates spending it, which is what a penny-pincher does.

clue.text: Puppet taken from girl by another heading off

indicators.note: with its heading off, the second girl's name loses its first letter

parts.note: a girl's name
another girl's name, as in Bette Davis

explanation.surface: A doll is snatched from one girl by another who then storms off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another girl: MARION followed by BETTE without its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a puppet worked by strings from above.

clue.text: Girl found in canal, an artiste

indicators.note: found in tells you the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: letters running across canal, an and artiste

explanation.surface: A girl is discovered in a canal along with a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alana is a girl's given name.

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night
a concert is a musical show

explanation.surface: Performers work together while a show is on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting' suggests the stage, which the show reinforces, but it means doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert is an idiom for cooperating or doing something together by agreement.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the novel by Elizabeth Gaskell
second meaning: the two players who sit opposite each other as a partnership at the card game

explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is the card game, not a crossing; its four seats are named after compass points, and the players opposite each other form partnerships.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaskell's 1855 novel has this title, and in bridge the seats facing each other are a partnership.

indicators.note: turned about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be taught about films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'on the subject of', but here it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The cinema is a collective term for films as an art form or industry, that is motion pictures.

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their letters are taken

parts.note: letters running across players, at and Zagreb

explanation.surface: A football substitute comes on from among the players at a match in Zagreb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior imitation used as a replacement, so it means substitute.

clue.text: The result of nurse's attention at the bedside?

definitions.text: The result of nurse's attention at the bedside?

parts.words: The result of nurse's attention at the bedside?
parts.note: surface reading: the outcome of a nurse caring for a patient; setter's reading: the neat folds a nurse makes in the sheets at the corners of a made bed

explanation.walkthrough: Bedside care suggests treating a patient, but the attention is paid to the bed itself and the tucked-in sheet corners.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital corners are tight, envelope-style folds of bedsheets, the method taught to nurses for making beds.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on the way, soon to arrive

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a synonym: oil travelling through a pipe
definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally inside a pipe used to carry oil

explanation.walkthrough: The second part is the literal sense of the idiom: oil flowing along a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes plans or goods already under way and soon to arrive, borrowing the image of oil flowing through a pipe.

clue.text: A wit badly described by brand new author

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw a line around, so the outer words enclose the rest
done badly, the letters come out in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: a brand is a trade mark
these letters are rearranged
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A clumsy joker is portrayed by a fresh brand of writer.
explanation.walkthrough: MARK and N together wrap around the rearranged A WIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of the American writer of Huckleberry Finn.

indicators.note: something amongst a group sits inside it, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a host is a great number, a crowd
the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is squashed among a crowd of people in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like the British word for an elevator, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise something up, typically with ropes or a mechanism, which is to lift it.

parts.note: tag is a children's chasing game
a team can be a pair yoked together, as of oxen

explanation.surface: Two wrestlers are described as a couple ready for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game couple' reads as a willing pair, but game is the playground game and couple is a yoked team.
explanation.definitionFit: In professional wrestling a tag team is a pair of partners who take turns in the ring.

clue.text: Soldier keeps an eye on bishop, say

parts.note: to guard is to watch over
a bishop is an example of a chessman, a piece in chess

explanation.surface: A soldier watches over a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop' suggests the church, but it is one of the pieces on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardsman is a soldier serving in a guards regiment.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the James Bond book by Ian Fleming
second meaning: a small sail set high above the skysail on a square-rigged ship

explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel sail' reads as an unusual piece of canvas, but Novel is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's 1955 Bond novel bears this title, and the name also belongs to a light topmost sail on old ships.

clue.text: Boy, one pecked by sea eagle

indicators.note: something pecked by a bird is gripped in its beak, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword regular
the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lad is attacked by a large coastal bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a boy's name, a familiar form of Ernest.

parts.note: surface reading: someone asking whether it is raining once more; setter's reading: two words spelt to look as though they rhyme, which only some speakers pronounce alike

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a rhyme on the page; only speakers who say the second word with a long A make them rhyme in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye rhyme is a pair of words whose spellings match at the end though their sounds differ, like rain and again.

clue.text: Mexican's mate in a plane close to Mexico

parts.note: taken as written
a MiG is a Russian-built fighter plane

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the country's name

explanation.surface: A Mexican's companion flies in an aircraft near the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, so it is the word a Mexican would use for a mate or pal.

clue.text: Unusually scanty clothing for all to see in Italian region

indicators.note: arranged unusually means the letters are not in their normal order
clothing something wraps around it, so the rearranged word goes around the other piece

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: Skimpy beachwear is on public display somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch, hence 'for all to see'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is a region of central Italy whose capital is Florence.

indicators.note: made short means the word is cut and loses its last letter

parts.note: RU is rugby union
a stick is a club or cudgel

explanation.surface: A basic sport is played with a shortened bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means plain and unsophisticated, in the manner of country life, hence simple.

clue.text: Inappropriate, a French affair of honour, unfinished

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: un is the French for a
a duel is fought to settle a point of honour

explanation.surface: A French duel left unresolved is deemed improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive or unwarranted, going beyond what is appropriate.

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
a runner is a kind of athlete

explanation.surface: A strange sportsman turns out to be a smuggler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like a description, but rum here is the old British word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum-runner smuggled alcohol, especially into the United States during Prohibition.

clue.text: One entering extremely modest French impressionist

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so one piece is placed within the other
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A very unassuming French painter of the impressionist school.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French painter whose Impression, Sunrise gave impressionism its name.

indicators.note: almost all of a word means it stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: normal means usual or typical

explanation.surface: An opera described as nearly run-of-the-mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is an opera by Bellini, famous for the aria Casta diva.

clue.text: Anyone march today? Drink needs to be ordered

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether anyone will march today, then orders a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom, Dick and Harry is an idiom for any ordinary person at all, so it means anyone.

clue.text: Bless sort of ancestor in church

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, so it is placed between the outer letters
a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters appear in another form

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A forebear of some kind is honoured with a blessing inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate is to make sacred with a religious rite, which is to bless.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: low, mean, without value
second meaning: the support a statue stands on

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a disdainful remark about a plinth, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Base is an adjective for low or worthless metal or morals, and a noun for the bottom support of something.
